analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read is caused by constructing `subs` via `table + table->substitutionTables` in `ContextualSubtable::driver_context_t` without validating that the 32-bit offset points to at least a readable `UnsizedOffsetListOf<Lookup<GlyphID>, HBUINT32>` header. During apply-time, malformed morx contextual subtable data can place this offset at/near the end of the blob; later `subs[index]` reads the first 2-byte offset field past allocation, crashing in `BEInt<unsigned short,2>::operator unsigned short()`. The crash site is generic integer load, but root cause is unsafe dereference of untrusted offset in contextual morx apply path.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In hb-shape-fuzzer, attacker-controlled font bytes (PoC includes a malformed AAT `mort`/`morx` contextual chain) reach `hb_aat_layout_substitute` -> `mortmorx::apply` -> `ContextualSubtable::apply`. The state machine triggers contextual substitution so `driver_context_t` is created and uses untrusted `substitutionTables` offset. If sanitize is bypassed/not enforced for this path or insufficient for this specific malformed layout, `subs` points out of bounds; then non-0xFFFF mark/current indices cause `subs[...]` access and a 2-byte OOB read at end of input buffer.
